chapters.title: Andhra Pradesh, year by year (all eras)
chapters.intro: Every Andhra event on the timeline, in one place — for Paper II Part B. It repeats the Andhra slides from the history and culture chapters, so you can revise Andhra history alone, from the Kurnool caves to the new state after 2014.

fragments.title: Prehistory to the Vishnukundins
fragments.intro: Jwalapuram, ash mounds, megaliths, Assaka, Ashoka's edicts, Bhattiprolu, Satavahanas, Amaravati, Ikshvakus and Vishnukundins.

fragments.title: Eastern Chalukyas to the Kakatiyas
fragments.intro: Vengi, Nannaya, Palnadu, the Kakatiyas, Rudramadevi and Marco Polo.

fragments.title: Reddis, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahis
fragments.intro: Musunuri Nayakas, Reddis, Srinatha, Annamacharya, Krishnadevaraya, Golconda, Hyderabad and the Europeans on the coast.

fragments.title: Company rule and the Telugu renaissance
fragments.intro: Northern Circars, poligars, Munro, Cotton, C.P. Brown, Veeresalingam and Gurajada.

fragments.title: The Andhra national movement
fragments.intro: Vandemataram, the Andhra Mahasabha, libraries, Alluri, Chirala-Perala, Pedanandipadu and the Telangana struggle.

fragments.title: Andhra State to the new Andhra Pradesh
fragments.intro: Potti Sriramulu, 1953, 1956, 1969, 1972, NTR, bifurcation in 2014 and after.

takeaways: Satavahanas → Ikshvakus → Vishnukundins → Eastern Chalukyas (624) → Kakatiyas (1163–1323) → Reddis and Musunuris → Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahis (1518–1687) → Nizams and the Company.
Andhra State 1 October 1953; Andhra Pradesh 1 November 1956; Telangana and residual AP 2 June 2014.
chapters.source: Andhra Pradesh history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus); NCERT (as cited on each event)
